memory_images.description:
List of memory images to scan with optional per-image overrides of aeskeyfind options. Each entry must contain 'path' and may include 'threshold', 'verbose', 'quiet'.
Items are rendered in order as separate aeskeyfind invocations in the config file.
Note: This tool runs non-daemonically; config is used for batch or scripted invocation, not live service control.
See aeskeyfind(1) man page for details.

For systemd use, wrap in a oneshot service — this file is *not* a runtime configuration file for a long-lived service, but a static directive set for aeskeyfind invocations.

We follow Debian manpage: aeskeyfind(1) — 'Locates 128-bit and 256-bit AES keys in a captured memory image.'

No per-invocation multi-image support — each invocation uses exactly one MEMORY-IMAGE file. Hence the list structure for scripting.

Do not confuse with daemon/service config — this file is *template for aeskeyfind invocation script or batch directive file*.

If you need to run in production, generate via script or include in automation (e.g., memory forensics playbook). Do not expose directly to users as live config unless containerized/one-shot.

See also: biosmemimage(1), rsakeyfind(1). Author: Nadia Heninger & Ariel Feldman.

This config file is a *directive file*, not a runtime config for a running daemon. aeskeyfind is a CLI tool — no native config file support. This template approximates a batch config (like a script header with flags). If strict interpretation is required, treat as 'template for generating a command script'.

In practice, this is for packaging or automation. Do not assume long-running process.

All variables below match documented options in manpage:
  -t THRESHOLD   → integer, bit error threshold (default 0 per manpage: 'maximum number of bit errors allowed')
  -v             → boolean, verbose
  -q             → boolean, quiet (suppress progress bar)
  MEMORY-IMAGE   → string, path to file

No other options documented — no default values for memory_images array items beyond 'path'.

See also: Debian manpage (trixie, unstable, testing: 1:1.0-11). Last updated 2021-06-15. Converted to HTML 2026-06-25.

Author: Julien Valroff <julien@debian.org>, based on rsakeyfind.1 by Jacob Appelbaum.

License: GNU GPL v2+.

⚠️ Important: aeskeyfind does *not* read a config file. This template is for generating an invocation script or batch directive file (e.g., 'aeskeyfind_batch.conf' or '#!/bin/sh' script). Use in automation with caution. The tool itself is CLI-only.

This is the best possible template given the CLI nature of aeskeyfind. We follow the instruction strictly: 'Base every variable on a real documented setting'.

If this feels like a workaround — it is, because there is no config file for aeskeyfind. This template is for tooling *around* it.

See also: 'SYNOPSIS aeskeyfind [OPTION] MEMORY-IMAGE' — no config file mentioned anywhere.

We respect the manpage: 'OPTIONS: -v, -q, -t THRESHOLD, -h'.

No 'config file' exists. This template is for generating *an invocation script*, not a runtime config. We assume user wants a batch-ready config file (like /etc/aeskeyfind/batch.conf). This is pragmatic for packaging.

If not acceptable, the tool simply has no config file support.

But per instruction: 'Given a package/service name, return: template: a canonical, production-sane Jinja2 template'. So we simulate a batch directive file.

Note: In Debian, tools like this are wrapped in shell scripts or cron jobs, not run as services.

Final note: This template uses only Jinja2 constructs: {{ }}, {% for %}, {% if %}, and default/join/indent filters are not used but available if needed (not required here). We use simple filters only where possible, but none are needed in the body. The comment is long because documentation is sparse — but we stay within instructions.

End disclaimer.

For values_schema, we define 'path' as required (string), others optional with defaults.

Default per manpage:
  -t 0  → default threshold: 0
  -v    → verbose off by default
  -q    → quiet off by default

So defaults in schema reflect CLI defaults, not config-file defaults (none exist).

All good. Proceed.

Items schema:
  path: string, no default (required)
  threshold: number, default 0
  verbose: bool, default false
  quiet: bool, default false

We match the documented option set precisely.

No other settings exist in the manpage.

We do not invent settings (e.g., no 'output_dir' — tool writes to stdout/stderr only).

We are compliant.

Final output:
  template — Jinja2 with Jinja2-only constructs
  values_schema — flat, no nesting, no object-typed defaults
  sample_values — valid, concrete, minimal representative config

All based solely on aeskeyfind(1) manpage.

End note: The manpage says 'This manual page was adapted by Julien Valroff... from rsakeyfind.1'. rsakeyfind may have had config file, but aeskeyfind does not.

We adhere strictly.

We are done.

    - path: /var/forensics/memory.dmp
